concept: A small working flywheel engine runs on a stone workbench. Beside it stand copies cast in solid bronze with no core: flawless, sharply detailed, every part fused, none of them able to turn. The original is worn, fingerprinted and oiled; the copies are immaculate because they have never worked. Beside the original lies an unfinished flywheel for the next engine.
theme: Authorship is maintenance, then the next build
quote: A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.
core_metaphor: A mold cast without a core records only the outside, so each copy is solid metal in a perfect silhouette. The original runs because its parts are separate, fitted, oiled and kept. The copy has the appearance of excellence; the original has the evidence of use.
emotional_arc: provocation -> respect for the copy -> distinction -> maintenance -> already building the next one
recurring_element: one canonical engine: a small single-cylinder horizontal mill engine on a worn stone workbench, black iron flywheel with six straight spokes turning clockwise as seen from camera at one steady speed in every shot; beside it one or more solid bronze copies of the same engine that never move
material: Original: aged brass (#C6A94F) cylinder, crosshead and valve gear, black iron six-spoke flywheel and bed; brass dulled at the edges, faint fingerprints, a fine oil sheen. Copies: solid dark bronze, crisp flawless detail, clean even patina, every joint fused, never handled. Worn charcoal stone bench in a near-black workshop; one cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and never moves
primary_prompt: Restrained photorealistic 9:16 sequence in one near-black stone workshop. On a worn charcoal stone bench a small single-cylinder flywheel engine of aged brass (#C6A94F) and black iron runs at one steady speed; its six-spoke flywheel turns clockwise, crank and piston rod linked. The brass is worn and fingerprinted with a thin oil sheen. Beside it stand flawless copies cast in solid dark bronze, every part fused, perfectly still. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and never moves. Locked or slow camera, real machined metal. No steam, no glow, no sparks, no lettering.

hook.text: Someone copied your work. Perfect copy. Dead engine.
hook.visual: Already in motion on the first frame: macro on the worn original's six-spoke black iron flywheel spinning clockwise, filling most of the frame, the brass crank flashing gold. The camera pulls back and slides right to the flawless bronze copy beside it, same outline, perfectly still, bone-white light on its flywheel rim.

build.text: They copied everything they could see. Every contour. Every detail.
build.visual: Slow lateral track along a row of solid bronze copies: crisp bolt heads, clean even patina, flawless and still, every joint fused. At the far end, soft in the background, the worn original's flywheel keeps turning.

pivot.text: A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.
pivot.visual: Macro on the original: the brass crosshead slides in its guide under a film of oil, the connecting rod drives the crank. Rack focus to the bronze copy beside it, same parts, one fused solid block.

resolution.text: Run your mind. Run your systems. Build the next one.
resolution.visual: Close on two hands, no face: a brass oil can drips into the oil cup on the crosshead guide; a fingerprint shows on the brass. The flywheel never changes speed. Beside it, an unfinished raw-iron six-spoke flywheel waits on the bench.

mobius_close.visual: Return to the opening frame: the worn engine turning beside the still bronze copy, same low angle and light. Nothing else changes. The flywheel rim catches a thin line of gold. Locked camera, matched for a seamless loop.

caption:
Someone copied your work. Perfect copy. Dead engine.

They copied everything they could see. Every contour. Every detail.

A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.

Run your mind. Run your systems. Build the next one.

And let them copy.
